result:
I fixed 11 rules in `pricebook.py` that didn't match their docstrings:

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 21, 72, 98, 116 | Marked "whole" but computed the discount only on units above the threshold | Discount now uses the full amount (`base`) |
| 54 | Rounded with `round` | Now rounds down to the won (`//`) |
| 62 | Cap only kicked in when the discount was over 200,000 | Cap of 100,000 now always applies |
| 74 | Capped the price instead of the discount | Cap now applies to the discount (100,000) |
| 80 | Capped the price instead of the discount | Cap now applies to the discount (30,000) |
| 83, 106 | Took 11% off | Changed to 10% |
| 92 | Discount started at 101 units | Now starts at 100 units |

Rule 50 checks `qty > 5` instead of `>= 5`, but it calculates the same amounts. At exactly 5 units no units are above the threshold, so the discount is 0 either way. I left it unchanged.

To check, I computed the expected price for all 150 rules from their docstrings and compared it with the code's result across many quantities and unit prices. No mismatches were left.

STATUS: DONE
